## Learning Objectives {.unnumbered}

## How it works

With the docker-uv-renv container running,
you can work inside it from Positron,
as if it were a remote Linux computer.
Positron's [Remote SSH](https://positron.posit.co/remote-ssh.html) documentation has the steps.
Here is how the pieces from the earlier chapters fit together:

- The image runs an ssh server when a container starts,
  because of its `CMD ["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D"]`
  (see [Python and R in one image](0648-containers-uv-renv.qmd)).
- `docker compose up --detach` starts the container in the background.
  Docker Compose maps port 2222 on your computer to the container's port 22,
  and mounts your ssh public key as the key that may log in as `root`
  (see [Docker Compose](0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd), including how to make a key).
- In Positron, run "Remote SSH: Show Remote Menu" from the Command Palette,
  pick "Connect to Host", and type `root@localhost:2222`.
  The first time, Positron installs its server inside the container,
  which takes a minute.
- Open the folder `/workspace`, which is your project folder.
  Positron's terminals, and its Python and R sessions, now run in the container.
- For Python, pick the interpreter `/opt/venv/bin/python`,
  the environment the image built from `uv.lock`.
  R uses the packages in `/opt/renv/library` without any setup,
  because of the `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` line in R's `Renviron.site`.
- An ssh login does not see the image's `ENV` settings,
  only the ones in `/etc/environment`.
  That is why the `Dockerfile` also writes `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` there,
  so that `uv` in a Positron terminal uses `/opt/venv` too.

## When it does not connect

These are the problems the docker-uv-renv README lists, and their fixes:

- `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` is a folder.
  Docker made it because the key did not exist when the container started.
  Run `docker compose down`, delete the folder, make the key,
  and run `docker compose up --detach` again.
- Your key has a different name.
  Change the key's path in `docker-compose.yml`.
- Positron or `ssh` says the remote host identification has changed.
  The container's ssh server has its own keys,
  which the image made when `apt-get` installed `openssh-server`.
  Rebuilding that step makes new ones,
  so your computer no longer recognizes the container.
  Forget the old key, then connect again:

  ```bash
  ssh-keygen -R "[localhost]:2222"
  ```
- On a Linux computer, the ssh server refuses the mounted key,
  because the file belongs to you, not to `root`.
  Uncomment the `StrictModes no` line in the `Dockerfile` and run `docker compose build`.

## An optional ssh shortcut

To type `ssh docker-uv-renv` instead of `ssh -p 2222 root@localhost`,
and to pick `docker-uv-renv` from a list in Positron,
add this to `~/.ssh/config` on your computer:

```
Host docker-uv-renv
  HostName localhost
  Port 2222
  User root
  StrictHostKeyChecking no
  UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null
```

The last two lines skip the host key check,
so that a rebuilt image does not cause the host key error above.
